title: Here's how I use AI to create my games (Claude + Cursor + UNITY)
author: forcegames
selftext:
Hey all, this is Gökhan.

I've been building games since 2013. Back then, there were no AI tools, no shortcuts, no one showing the way. I had to learn everything on my own, from scratch.

Over the years, I built [Trifles Games](https://www.loom.com/share/a9be14c7a1164c169e1193965ade1103) from nothing. I set up an office in the heart of Istanbul, grew a team from 1 to 29 people, published dozens of games, and partnered with companies like **Rollic** and **Homa Games.**

In 2023, at just **27 years old**, I was selected for [Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/profile/gokhan-kinay/). Not because I got lucky. Because I never, ever stopped.

But if I'm being honest? The hardest part was never the work. It was the loneliness..

Having no one to ask for help. No one to tell me if I was even on the right path. Sending messages that were never answered. Knocking on doors that stayed shut.

I built this community because I wish it existed when I needed it most.

**I figured it all out alone. You don't have to.**

Inside, you won't find recycled theory or generic tutorials. You'll see exactly how a real game studio operates. How we build games, how we ship them, and how we actually earn from them. Every decision, every step, nothing hidden.

And now, with AI changing everything, you'll see firsthand how we use these new tools in our actual workflow to build faster and smarter than ever.

Because the future of game dev isn't about who writes the cleanest code..   
  
**It's about who uses AI to build and ship 10x faster.**

..and I'm dropping the link to watch the live call recording above:

**Full recording link:** [https://futureofgamedev.com](https://futureofgamedev.com)

Here's what we talked about in the live call:

\- Unity MCP

\- Claude AI (Coding)

\- Cursor AI (Coding)

\- Tripo AI (3d model)

\- Whisk - Google Labs (2d concept)

P.S. I truly believe AI won't replace game developers. **But devs who use AI will.** 

We just need to adapt to the new era. Because traditional game dev is becoming too slow and too expensive. AI is no longer a "maybe".. 

Think back to the Atari days, then look at modern PC gaming. The next evolution is agentic coding with AI.

P.P.S. To be clear, I’m not talking about AI slop games or vibe coding... It’s the exact opposite. This is about indie devs shipping faster with leaner teams. Imagine orchestrating 4-5 AI agents at once.

 I'd love to hear your thoughts.

comments.author: Otherwise_Wave9374
comments.body:
The 4-5 agents orchestration point is the part that feels like the real shift, not just autocomplete code.

In game dev especially, Ive seen people get better results when they split roles: one agent as planner/PM, one as gameplay code implementer, one as tests/QA, and one as content/polish, with tight checklists between them. Otherwise it turns into one big fuzzy chat.

Curious what you use as the glue, is it just prompts, or do you have a lightweight agent framework to manage tasks and handoffs?

If youre into agent workflows, this blog has a few solid posts on building reliable AI agents: https://www.agentixlabs.com/blog/

replies.author: forcegames
replies.body:
Hi, thanks for the comment. AI won't replace us, it'll just let us get more done with a smaller team. It’s all about making everything faster.

Right now, I’m building different agents to handle planning, coding, art, and builds (xcode, etc). But thanks for the blog link.

And it feels good to stop writing loops manually and let AI speed everything up. We’d love to have anyone interested in AI game dev in our community, thanks.

To me, this whole AI debate feels exactly like the **Manual vs. Automatic transmission** situation. Back then, everyone said, 'Real drivers use a manual stick!' or 'You don't have control if it’s an automatic!' replies.author: forcegames

[https://www.linkedin.com/posts/gokhankinay\_i-was-dead-broke-my-father-went-bankrupt-activity-7415324202431516672-aQHu](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/gokhankinay_i-was-dead-broke-my-father-went-bankrupt-activity-7415324202431516672-aQHu)

This is my life story. By the time I made it into Forbes at 27, I had a 14-person team and my own office in Istanbul. But I went through some incredibly tough times, and nobody was there to help me.

Now, I’m posting on Reddit specifically because I want to help others, and seeing these kinds of comments is honestly disheartening.

AI isn't going to take anyone’s job in gaming industry. It’s exactly like the shift from BlackBerry’s physical keys to the iPhone’s touchscreen. It just makes life easier and speeds up the process, that’s it. I really don’t understand why there is so much hate towards AI.

comments.author: HONGSHIreddit
comments.body:
I honestly believe AI will be the new modern day standard going forward. Like any other tool we use, AI will be just that, a TOOL. I'm not a coder but I would say I'm a decent graphic artist and beginner 3D modeler and thanks to AI, Bezi in particular, I was able to participate in a game jam and actually start and finish (somewhat) a project. I was able to learn and research different programming patterns, best, practices, and other game development concepts and apply them using Bezi as a tool for learning and code my game projects.

Sure, there are a lot of slop out there made with AI but that's up to the individual who uses the AI to create slop. Just like people can use Google translate to create sloppy translations and call it a day, people will use AI to generate slop, upload, and call it a day. But if an individual were to use Google translate and fix some of the parts that are incorrect, then they have a good baseline with minor fixes ready to post. I also believe this is the case with the AI. 

Artists do this all the time. And I'm not talking about those AI generated art slop that people post either. I'm talking about artists who generate different types of images and references for themselves and use those references to create their own stuff. You just don't know it because they're actually posting their original work while using AI art as reference. They also do this to create and generate their own mood boards if they can't find anything on Pinterest or Google.

So I hope people will stop saying AI is bad and it ruins everything sooner rather than later because I feel that it isn't going anywhere. So rather than thinking AI is bad. Use it to your advantage and get a leg up on everyone else.

replies.author: forcegames
replies.body:
Thank you, and I totally agree with you.

Using AI as a **TOOL** rather than just a shortcut for 'slop' is the way to go. Your experience with Bezi is a perfect example. It’s not about letting the AI do everything, it’s about lowering the technical bar so your creativity can actually come to life. And congrats on the game jam!

In my opinion, the reason people call AI 'bad' or say it 'ruins everything' is mostly because they only see the low-effort 'slop' and assume that’s all the tool can do. There’s also a lot of gatekeeping, some feel like if you didn't spend years struggling with manual coding, you didn't 'earn' the right to make a game. 

But that's just noise. Because AI is a massive **efficiency boost**, not a replacement for talent.

Your experience with Bezi proves exactly that. It helped you bridge the gap between your art skills and technical execution. You aren't 'cheating'.. You’re just being a smarter director of your own vision.

To me, this whole AI debate feels exactly like the **Manual vs. Automatic transmission** situation. Back then, everyone said, 'Real drivers use a manual stick!' or 'You don't have control if it’s an automatic!' Now, almost everyone drives an automatic because it's just smarter and easier, especially in traffic.

It's the same situation in the AI era. AI is just a TOOL helping you out, nothing more. It doesn't replace your vision. **It just handles the 'shifting' so you can focus on the road.**

replies.author: HONGSHIreddit
replies.body:
I love the whole manual vs transmission analogy lol

I believe we're in the growing pain stages of AI but sooner or later, it'll regulate itself and I'm sure everyone will not even talk about it like we are now because it'll be part of everyday life. 

So I would use this time to get good at using the tool so you guys can get ahead of the curve. But like everything else, just because you have the tools doesn't mean you know how to use it effectively. You can give me all the lumber, hammer and nails but it doesn't mean I know how to make a house. Still takes time and knowledge to get results
